<section id="why" class="alt">
  <div class="wrap">
    <h2>Why have a website of your own?</h2>
    <div class="why-grid">
      <div>
        <h3>Recruit</h3>
        <p>Applicants look you up before they apply. Give them a clear picture of your group and your open positions.</p>
      </div>
      <div>
        <h3>Be found</h3>
        <p>Collaborators, journalists and funders find a current story instead of a stale profile page.</p>
      </div>
      <div>
        <h3>Share openly</h3>
        <p>Link every paper to its data, code and DOI, so your open science is visible.</p>
      </div>
      <div>
        <h3>Stay current</h3>
        <p>Updating takes minutes, so the site keeps pace with your group.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<section id="how" class="alt">
  <div class="wrap">
    <h2>How it works</h2>
    <ol class="process">
      <li>
        <span class="n">1</span>
        <h3>Intro call</h3>
        <p>We talk about your work and who the site is for.</p>
      </li>
      <li>
        <span class="n">2</span>
        <h3>Send your content</h3>
        <p>You get one checklist for texts, photos and publications. I build, and you review a draft link.</p>
      </li>
      <li>
        <span class="n">3</span>
        <h3>Launch and handover</h3>
        <p>Your site goes live and I show your team how to update it. Most sites take about two weeks.</p>
      </li>
    </ol>

</section>

<section id="pricing">
  <div class="wrap">
    <h2>Pricing</h2>
    <p class="lede" style="margin-top:16px">One-time fees, no subscriptions.</p>
    <div class="plans">
      <div class="plan">
        <span class="tag">&nbsp;</span>
        <h3>Researcher</h3>
        <div class="price">[PRICE] <small>SEK</small></div>
        <p>A personal site for PhD students, postdocs and PIs: about, CV, publications and profile links.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="plan featured">
        <span class="tag">Most chosen</span>
        <h3>Research group</h3>
        <div class="price">[PRICE] <small>SEK</small></div>
        <p>Research, people, publications, news and open positions, with a handover session and update guide.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="plan">
        <span class="tag">&nbsp;</span>
        <h3>Project</h3>
        <div class="price"><small>from</small> [PRICE] <small>SEK</small></div>
        <p>For EU projects and research networks: partners, outputs, events and funder acknowledgements.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <p class="fine">Prefer to email changes instead of editing files? Add a care plan for [PRICE] SEK per year.</p>
  </div>
</section>

<section id="faq" class="alt">
  <div class="wrap">
    <h2>Questions</h2>
    <div class="faq">
      <details>
        <summary>Can a grant pay for this?</summary>
        <p>Often, yes. A website can count as a dissemination cost, especially in EU projects. Your grant administrator can confirm for your funder.</p>
      </details>
      <details>
        <summary>We already have a university page. Why add a site?</summary>
        <p>A site of your own has room for your story, team, news and open positions, and it links back to your official page.</p>
      </details>
      <details>
        <summary>What if nobody on our team knows GitHub?</summary>
        <p>You get a step-by-step guide and a handover session. Most updates happen in the browser, by editing a short text file.</p>
      </details>
      <details>
        <summary>Who owns the site?</summary>
        <p>You do. It lives in your own GitHub account, so nothing is locked in and nothing breaks if we stop working together.</p>
      </details>
      <details>
        <summary>Can we use our own domain?</summary>
        <p>Yes. I set it up for you, and the domain stays registered in your name.</p>
      </details>
      <details>
        <summary>Is this only for the life sciences?</summary>
        <p>No. From biology to sociology, any field is welcome.</p>
      </details>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
